papers.title_in_file: Maximum-Entropy Inference with a Programmable Annealer
papers.version_note: arXiv:1506.08140v2 (1 Mar 2016) with the supplemental material; the text layer carries the main paper, supplement and references once. Flat exponents (2N+M, Nsamp = 105, 5 105) lost their superscripts, and Eq. 4 and several relation signs are garbled.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental D-Wave Vesuvius study of maximum entropy (finite temperature) decoding of an Ising-code on Chimera graphs, with a spin-by-spin test of how Boltzmann-like the annealer's samples are.

assertions.value: The authors report that all decoding experiments ran on the D-Wave Vesuvius processor at the Information Sciences Institute of the University of Southern California, which has 512 bits in an 8x8 array of unit cells, and that the annealing time was 20µs.

quotes: Sciences Institute of the University of Southern California. This processor contains 512 bits in an 8x8
with tf = 20µs

assertions.value: The paper defines two generic approaches to drawing a conclusion from incomplete or noisy measurements: maximum a priori (MAP) estimation, which gives a unique conclusion that maximises the likelihood of being correct, and marginal posterior maximisation (MPM), which gives a probabilistic conclusion whose distribution maximises entropy.
quotes: maximum a priori (MAP) estimation, which results in a unique conclusion which maximises the likelihood of being correct;
marginal posterior maximisation (MPM), which results in a probabilistic conclusion whose distribution maximises entropy.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the two approaches in its Introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that the maximum entropy MPM approach is an implementation of Bayesian inference since prior knowledge about the expected distribution of the measurements is required.
quotes: The maximum entropy MPM approach is an implementation of Bayesian inference since prior knowledge about the expected distribution of the measurements is required.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this in its Introduction as framing.

assertions.value: The authors report from the exhaustive-sum analytical model that at low Nishimori temperature (low channel noise) the Bayesian approach fares badly compared with maximum likelihood, and that as channel noise increases the maximum entropy approach outperforms ground state decoding for the quadratic Hamiltonian used, from which they conclude that qualitatively the D-Wave machine behaves as a maximum entropy decoder.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the single unit cell no spins show more than one spin-sign transition at finite temperature, so the transition plot is a valid way to analyse decoding at any temperature without considering errors from multiple transitions.
quotes: It is important that, in the case of the single unit cell, there are no spins which show more than one spin-sign transition at ﬁnite temperature.
The transition plot should therefore be a valid way to analyze the decoding at any temperature
assertions.certainty_reason: A computed property of the single-cell family, stated without the enumeration shown.

assertions.value: The authors state that the spin-sign transition temperatures for the 4x4 chimera graph with 128 qubits cannot be found by exhaustive search but are found using bucket tree elimination (BTE), and that spins with a ground state orientation of zero are excluded because statistical error would produce spurious transitions.
assertions.anchor: Microscopic theory, p.10; Supplement Sec. 4, p.15
quotes: While the calculation of the spin-sign transition temperatures cannot be performed by exhaustive search the way the single unit cell was, it can be eﬃciently solved using a bucket tree elimination (BTE) [56].
For spins with a ground state orientation of zero, the orientation curve as a function of T remains very close to zero at low temperatures.
For this reason we exclude these data from our analysis.
For this purpose, we consider a 4x4 chimera graph with 128 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its method and exclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the D-Wave supplied BTE code acts as a fair Boltzmann sampler giving an unbiased sample of Nsamp spin states at a given temperature, that they use Nsamp = 105 (the exponent is printed flat in the text layer), sample 200 temperatures between T = 0 and T = 7, then take a running average over 5 neighbouring points and use linear interpolation to find zero crossings.
quotes: This code acts as a fair Boltzmann sampler and can be made to provide an unbiased sample of Nsamp spin states at a given temperature T .
We use Nsamp = 105.
We then sample 200 temperatures between T = 0 and T = 7 to determine spin orientations.
by ﬁrst taking a running average over 5 neighboring points to suppress multiple spurious transitions and then using linear interpolation to ﬁnd the zero crossings.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its computational method.

assertions.value: The authors state that when the ground state orientation is zero and the orientation stays very close to zero over a wide temperature range, statistical sampling error makes their method find spurious transitions, so these spins are excluded from the analysis.
quotes: statistical sampling error leads to this method ﬁnding spurious transitions. Because of these spurious transitions these spins are excluded from our analysis.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own exclusion rule.

assertions.value: The paper defines two performance measures for the larger system: Perr(T), the average over Hamiltonians of the disagreement between the Boltzmann-predicted decoding and the experimental result at the same temperature, and, allowing different Hamiltonians to freeze at different times, the minimum over T of that error for each Hamiltonian individually; only bits with at least one spin-sign transition are included.
quotes: First we can compare all Hamiltonians with a Boltzmann distribution at the same temperature,
Second we admit the possibilities that diﬀerent Hamiltonians freeze at diﬀerent times and examine minT (PeHrr(T )) for each Hamiltonian individually.
we only include bits with at least one spin-sign transition in this analysis to avoid the data being overwhelmed by spins
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its metrics.

assertions.value: The authors report that the single-cell data in Fig. 6 show the device should perform maximum entropy tasks quite well, but that in both plots the transition is significantly broader than the pure Boltzmann result, which they most likely attribute to control errors causing random deviations in the couplers and fields.
quotes: The data plotted in Fig. 6 demonstrate that for this example the device should perform maximum entropy tasks quite well.
in both plots the transition is signiﬁcantly broader than the pure Boltzmann result.
This eﬀect can most likely be attributed to control errors, which cause random deviations in the couplers and the ﬁelds.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device; the control-error attribution is an author conjecture at this point.

assertions.value: The authors report that especially in Fig. 6 b) some individual transitions decode correctly but deviate strongly from what a Boltzmann sampler would give, say these could be due to dynamical effects like those explored in cited work, and note the associated Hamiltonians may warrant future study.
assertions.anchor: Microscopic results, p.11; Supplement Sec. 5, p.15-16
quotes: there are some individual transitions which decode correctly but deviate strongly from what we would expect from a Boltzmann sampler.
These could be due to dynamical eﬀects similar to the ones explored in [55].
the Hamiltonians associated with these transitions may warrant future study.
It is also worth noting that especially in 6 b) there are some individual transitions which decode correctly
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation from one device with a speculative cause.

assertions.value: The authors report that fitting the Boltzmann form to the single-cell data gives a fitted temperature of Tfit = 0.170 J for α = 0.05 and Tfit = 0.175 J for α = 0.1.
quotes: a) α = 0.05; in this case the ﬁtted temperature is Tfit = 0.170 J. b) α = 0.1; in this case the ﬁtted temperature is Tfit = 0.175 J .

assertions.value: The authors report that the system appears to freeze earlier for larger α, that the small difference in apparent temperature corresponds to freezing at a much higher transverse field, and that in all cases the transverse field at the freeze time is much weaker than the couplers.

Although the diﬀerence in apparent temperature is relatively small, it corresponds to freezing with a much higher value of transverse ﬁeld.
in all cases the transverse ﬁeld at the freeze time is much weaker than the couplers.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result derived from fits on one device.

Data are based on 145 randomly chosen Hamiltonians with 200 ﬂipped bonds or ﬁelds. For each Hamiltonian 100 sets of 1000 annealing cycles are performed.

assertions.value: The authors state that the top panel is bucket tree elimination sampled over independent control error of 5% J in the fields and 3% J in the couplers (perfect equilibration subject to control error), and the bottom panel is simulated annealing with 10,000 total updates, no control error, a linear sweep starting from T /(αJ) = 10 and 1000 samples per run.
quotes: bucket tree elimination sampled over independent control error of 5% J in the ﬁelds and 3% J in the couplers.
Simulated Annealing (SA) with 10,000 total updates and no control error.
These data were taken with a linear sweep starting from T /(αJ) = 10.
These data were calculated based on 1000 samples per run as were used experimentally.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its simulation settings.

assertions.value: The authors report that limiting simulated annealing to 10,000 updates makes failure to equilibrate produce a signature in which spins consistently decode with an orientation different from Boltzmann expectation, that this signature is not observed experimentally, which they say suggests the device is reaching equilibrium, and that the experimental data show a clear signature of control error, a broadening of the transition.
quotes: By limiting the simulation to a total of 10,000 updates we see that failure to equilibrate produces a signature in which spins consistently decode with an orientation
We do not observe this signature experimentally, which suggests that the device is in fact reaching equilibrium,
Our experimental data do however display a clear signature of control error
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the inference of equilibrium rests on absence of a simulated signature.

assertions.value: The authors note that the simulated annealing transition in Fig. 8b is apparently shifted to a lower temperature, suspect this is because the local minima in which the simulation is trapped correspond to an effectively lower temperature, and say further investigation is beyond the scope of the work.
quotes: The astute reader will note that Fig. 8b) demonstrates a transition which is apparently shifted to a lower temperture.
such an investigation is beyond the scope of this work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states an open item and its scope.

assertions.value: The authors report in the supplement that for a randomly selected 128-bit Hamiltonian a linear sweep from T /(αJ) = 10 to T /(αJ) = 1.405 maintains equilibrium (as found by BTE) with 1,000,000 updates but fails to maintain it with 10,000 updates, with the 10,000-update data deviating significantly from equilibrium at a T /(αJ) value of 3.5 (the relation sign is lost in the text layer).

throughout the entire sweep if 1,000,000 updates are used, but fails to maintain equilibrium if only 10,000 are used
With only 10,000 updates the SA data begin to signiﬁcantly deviate from thermal equilibrium at T /(αJ) 3.5,
for a randomly selected 128 bit Hamiltonian from our data,

These data were taken with a linear sweep starting from T /(αJ) = 5 with 5 105 samples, 5% ﬁeld control errors and 3% coupler control error.
Each randomly generated instance of the error was run for 100 annealing runs and 100 instances were considered for each Hamiltonian.

assertions.value: The authors state that the performance metrics are better for larger α by all measures, consistent with control errors being the limiting factor because at smaller α the control errors are more significant compared with the Hamiltonian energy scale, and that a limit from failure to reach equilibrium would be expected to give the opposite trend because smaller energy barriers make equilibrium easier.
quotes: The table shows better performance by all metrics for larger values of α, again consistent with control errors being the limiting factor
if the performance were limited because the dynamics were unable to reach equilibrium than we would expect to see the opposite trend,
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical trend over three α values on one device; the attribution is an inference by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that maximum entropy approaches to decoding on the D-Wave chip programmable Josephson junction annealer can give somewhat improved accuracy, which they say confirms that useful information can be extracted from the excited states at the end of the annealing process.
quotes: We have shown that maximum entropy approaches to decoding, implemented using the D-Wave chip programmable Josephson junction annealer, can result in somewhat improved accuracy.
We show experimentally that ﬁnite temperature maximum entropy decoding can give slightly better bit-error-rates than the maximum likelihood approach,
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one device; the paper says 'somewhat' and 'slightly'.

assertions.value: The authors conclude from the spin-level analysis that the experimental device produces a distribution that is Boltzmann like and suitable for maximum entropy tasks, and that the most probable limiting factors are control errors rather than equilibration dynamics.
quotes: the experimental device produces a distribution which is Boltzmann like and therefore suitable for maximum entropy tasks.
we demonstrate that the most probable limiting factors for such tasks are control errors, rather than equilibration dynamics.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical conclusion from one device, with an author inference about the cause.

assertions.value: The authors claim their results are applicable to a wide range of machine learning and optimisation problems provided prior information is known, that applications where maximum likelihood performs poorly or marginal benefits are valuable would suit the current two-local D-Wave architecture, and that an architecture with m-local couplers (m >= 3) would allow the Shannon limit to be approached in decoding.
quotes: Our results are applicable to a wide range of problems in machine learning and optimization provided knowledge of prior information.
would be most suited to the current D-Wave architecture which features two-local couplers.
An extension of the architecture to allow m-local couplers (with m ≥ 3) would allow the Shannon limit to be approached in decoding applications[57].
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim of applicability without an ML task run in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Only a decoding task was run; no machine learning application was tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that their work treats the D-Wave processor as a classical thermal annealing device, and that more experiments, for example varying the annealing schedule, would be needed to determine the role, if any, of quantum fluctuations on maximum entropy inference with it.
quotes: While our work has focused on the exploitation of the D-wave processor as a classical thermal annealing device,
to determine the role (if any) of quantum ﬂuctuations on maximum entropy inference using the D-Wave processor would be illuminating.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states a limit on what its experiments establish.

assertions.value: The authors state in the abstract that the annealer samples from a highly Boltzmann-like distribution, and that machines of this kind are therefore candidates for machine learning applications that exploit maximum entropy inference, including language processing and image recognition.
quotes: use it to show that the annealer samples from a highly Boltzmann-like distribution.
Machines of this kind are therefore candidates for use in a variety of machine learning applications which exploit maximum entropy inference,
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; no language or image task is run.
